result.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning
result.summary: Recent Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) use Self-Conditioning (SC), or Loopholing, to improve their performance. While SC is traditionally seen as an auxiliary heuristic, its empirical success raises the question: can a continuous generative model be based purely on Self-Conditioning? We answer affirmatively with LAW (``Loopholing All the Way''), which propagates the Expected Embedding under the denoiser's prediction across steps, decoding the tokens once, at the end. On Sudoku, LAW outperforms previous Discrete and Continuous Diffusion Models, including Loopholing Discrete Diffusion. On Maze, LAW is the most accurate from 2 to 64 NFE. After training on TinyGSM and sampling at temperature 1 with 1024 NFE, LAW solves 42.2% of GSM8K problems against 34.5% for uniform Loopholing Discrete Diffusion. Additionally, fine-tuning a pre-trained Uniform Diffusion Model (Duo) with LAW increases its accuracy from 17.2% to 48.1%. Finally, on OpenWebText, LAW pushes the Pareto frontier and approaches Autoregressive Models (ARMs) with 64 NFE. Find our code at https://github.com/ilievanadezhda/law.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LAW，把扩散语言模型中的 Self-Conditioning（Loopholing）由辅助启发式升级为纯生成机制：在去噪器预测下跨步传播期望 embedding，仅在最后一次性解码 token，并在 Sudoku、Maze、TinyGSM/GSM8K 与 OpenWebText 上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其连续状态跨步传播、末端单次解码以及 NFE 与精度的权衡，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的更新方式与解码时机；但该工作为纯文本扩散，缺少视觉多模态验证，迁移性仍是推测。
